title: HLS Stream
tagline: Production-grade HLS video streaming platform with microservices architecture, adaptive bitrate delivery, and creator analytics.

caseStudy.problem: Centralized video platforms impose upload limits, algorithmic suppression, and opaque analytics. Developers and creators need a self-hosted, production-ready alternative with full control over transcoding pipelines, storage, and delivery — without sacrificing streaming performance.
caseStudy.solution: A containerized, microservices-based video platform where uploaded videos are automatically transcoded into HLS segments via FFmpeg workers, stored on AWS S3, and streamed with adaptive bitrate delivery. Role-based access spans creators, moderators, and admins through a unified Next.js frontend.
architecture: User Management Service (Node.js + JWT): handles registration, email verification, role assignment, and avatar upload.
Video Upload Service: receives raw files (MP4, AVI, MOV, WMV), validates format, and enqueues transcoding jobs via Redis queue.
Transcoding Orchestration Service: dispatches jobs to Docker-based FFmpeg workers; manages concurrency, retries, and progress events.
Transcoding Workers: isolated containers running FFmpeg — produce multi-resolution HLS playlists (.m3u8) and segment files (.ts), then push to S3.
Video Streaming Service: serves HLS manifests and segments from S3 with signed URLs; supports adaptive bitrate switching.
Video Metadata Service: PostgreSQL-backed store for titles, descriptions, thumbnails, view counts, and creator associations.
Notification Service: real-time event delivery (upload complete, new subscriber) via WebSocket or polling.
Next.js Frontend: creator dashboard with analytics, admin panel, and an HLS.js-powered video player.
decisions: Chose HLS over DASH: broader native browser/device support and simpler CDN caching of static .ts segments.
Redis-backed job queue over direct service calls: decouples upload latency from transcoding duration — uploads return instantly, workers process async.
Docker workers for FFmpeg: each transcoding job runs in an isolated container, preventing resource contention and allowing independent horizontal scaling.
AWS S3 for segment storage: eliminates disk I/O bottleneck on streaming nodes; signed URLs enforce access control without a media proxy.
PostgreSQL over NoSQL: relational schema fits video-user-subscription relationships cleanly; analytics queries benefit from JOIN and aggregation support.
challenges: Orchestrating job state across Upload → Orchestrator → Worker → Metadata pipeline required a shared event schema in Redis to avoid race conditions on concurrent uploads.
FFmpeg multi-resolution output (e.g., 1080p, 720p, 480p) dramatically increases S3 write volume — batched multipart uploads and per-resolution worker parallelism were used to contain latency.
Kubernetes readiness probes needed careful tuning for FFmpeg worker pods, which have high startup cost but long idle periods between jobs.
caseStudy.metrics_detail: 7+ independent microservices across upload, transcoding, streaming, metadata, notification, user management, and frontend layers. Kubernetes manifests + Terraform configs included for production deployment. Prometheus metrics exposed per service; Grafana dashboards monitor transcoding queue depth, active streams, and error rates.

title: AgriChain
tagline: End-to-end agricultural supply chain on Ethereum with AI-driven insurance risk scoring.

caseStudy.problem: Agricultural supply chains in India suffer from opacity — farmers receive 20-30% of final product value due to multi-layer middlemen, and banks cannot verify crop ownership or yield history for loan underwriting.
caseStudy.solution: A permissioned DApp on Ethereum where each produce batch is minted as an on-chain asset. Role-based smart contracts enforce ownership transfers across Farmer → Vendor → Consumer.
architecture: Solidity contracts (Truffle) manage asset lifecycle: mint, transfer, verify, insure.
React frontend with Web3.js connects MetaMask wallet and dispatches contract calls.
TensorFlow.js model runs client-side for crop health inference.
Flask microservice handles VGG19-based risk scoring and generates PDF insurance reports.
Firebase Firestore stores off-chain metadata linked by IPFS content hash.
decisions: Chose Ethereum + Truffle over Hyperledger: simpler local dev cycle, better React/Web3.js tooling.
Client-side TF.js for lightweight checks avoids latency for farmers with poor connectivity.
Role-based access enforced in Solidity modifiers — not just frontend gates.
challenges: Gas cost optimization for batch minting: consolidated struct packing reduced deployment cost by ~18%.
Coordinating 5 distinct role dashboards from a single contract state required careful event indexing.
caseStudy.metrics_detail: VGG19 crop disease model: 91% test accuracy on 38-class PlantVillage dataset. Contract functions: 14 public entry points across 3 contracts.

title: CropMD
tagline: Computer vision diagnostic portal for crop and livestock disease — Flask + VGG19 inference pipeline.

caseStudy.problem: Smallholder farmers in India lose 15-25% of crop yield annually to undiagnosed disease. Access to trained agronomists is limited and expensive.
caseStudy.solution: A web portal where farmers upload a leaf image. The backend runs it through a fine-tuned VGG19 pipeline, returns disease name, confidence score, and a structured treatment plan as a downloadable PDF.
architecture: Flask REST API receives base64 image, preprocesses to 224x224 for VGG19 input.
VGG19 fine-tuned on PlantVillage dataset with transfer learning from ImageNet weights.
Prediction + top-3 confidence scores returned with mapped treatment metadata.
Firebase Storage for image persistence; Firestore for diagnosis history per session.
decisions: VGG19 over MobileNet: higher accuracy on fine-grained disease patterns — acceptable for server-side inference.
Treatment metadata stored as JSON lookup — disease classes are finite and rarely change.
challenges: Class imbalance in PlantVillage mitigated with class-weighted loss during fine-tuning.
Image quality from mobile cameras required CLAHE contrast enhancement preprocessing.
caseStudy.metrics_detail: 91% top-1 accuracy, 97% top-3 accuracy across 38 disease classes. Inference: 380ms avg. Report generation under 2 seconds.

title: VoiceCart
tagline: Voice-to-product search assistant with live e-commerce link generation.

caseStudy.problem: Voice commerce interfaces either use rigid keyword matching or dump raw transcriptions into search bars. The result is high error rates and user abandonment.
caseStudy.solution: A React app that listens via Web Speech API, sends transcript to OpenAI intent parser extracting product category, attributes, and price constraints, then assembles deep-link search URLs per platform.
architecture: Web Speech API handles real-time transcription with interim results for live feedback.
Node.js middleware forwards transcript to OpenAI with structured extraction prompt.
URL builder maps parsed intent to platform-specific query parameters.
React state machine manages: idle → listening → processing → results → error.
decisions: OpenAI for intent parsing over regex: generalizes to colloquial queries rule-based systems fail on.
State machine over ad-hoc booleans: voice UIs have complex async transitions.
challenges: Web Speech API fires multiple interim events — debouncing required careful timing logic.
Cross-browser support gaps required feature detection with text-input fallback.
caseStudy.metrics_detail: End-to-end query parse time: median 780ms on broadband. Text fallback covers ~15% of sessions.
